title: Square sums of Pell numbers
summary: Add the first 4n + 1 positive-index Pell numbers. The result is always a square, for example 1 + 2 + 5 + 12 + 29 = 49.

tasks.title: Telescope the Pell prefix
tasks.claim:
∀ n : ℕ, 2 * (∑ k ∈ Finset.range (4 * n + 1), pell (k + 1)) + 1 =
    pell (4 * n + 2) + pell (4 * n + 1)
tasks.role: Expresses twice the target sum plus one in terms of its endpoints.
tasks.context: Prove the identity first for an arbitrary prefix length m, with right side P(m+1) + P(m). On extending the prefix by one, the right side increases by 2P(m+1) by the Pell recurrence. The empty prefix gives 1 on both sides.

tasks.title: Identify the square at the endpoint
tasks.role: Expresses the same endpoint expression using the proposed square root.
tasks.context: Write Q(j) = P(j+1) − P(j) over the integers. The recurrence gives Q(j+1) = Q(j) + 2P(j) and P(j+1) = Q(j) + P(j). By induction on j, Q(j)^2 − 2P(j)^2 = (−1)^j. The same recurrences give Q(2j) = Q(j)^2 + 2P(j)^2 by multiplication of Q + P√2. Hence Q(4n+2) = 2Q(2n+1)^2 + 1. Use P(j+2) − P(j+1) = P(j+1) + P(j) to translate back.
